messages:
sam: heads-up — multiple CI pipelines started failing ~20m ago when trying to fetch secrets with the CI service account. error from token exchange looks like: 

```
2026-03-15T10:42:01Z ERROR auth: token exchange failed: 401 Unauthorized - id_token expired (exp: 1670000000)
pipeline: gitlab-runner/runner-42 -> fetching secret project/my-app/staging
```

sam: this is blocking all staging deploys. I tried re-running a couple jobs and same result. no config changes in the repo AFAIK. pinging infra and support. @irina can you take a look?

jessie: looking. do you have the raw oidc assertion or runner logs? sometimes it's clock skew or the runner's short-lived token TTL.

sam: runner log attached below (redacted):

```
level=info msg="requesting id_token" runner=gitlab-r1
level=debug msg="id_token received" exp=3600 issuer=https://gitlab.example.com
level=warn msg="token accepted by upstream failed" status=401 reason="token expired"
```

jessie: hmmm. two possibilities: 1) the runner is generating a token with a very short lifetime (e.g. 30s) and our token validator sees it as expired by the time it reaches the exchange service, OR 2) there's clock skew between runner host and our auth service. can you check NTP on the runner host?

irina: checked NTP on the runner node — time is within 2s of ntp pool. not a skew. I pulled the id_token claim from one of the failed runs; `iat` is 2026-03-15T10:41:10Z, `exp` is 2026-03-15T10:41:40Z (30s TTL). GitLab runner config shows `oidc_id_token_lifetime: 30s` in the helm chart for this cluster (values override from infra team).

irina: so the token is very short-lived. the exchange service expects at least 60s buffer for processing because we validate timestamps and sign checks. 30s TTL is too aggressive for network latency + proxy hops.

mike: security note — increasing TTL increases risk window for impersonation. we should avoid making it huge. options:
- allow short token but accept tokens with small clock skew (adjust validator tolerance to 10s)
- increase runner token TTL to 60s or 90s (preferred minimal change)
- change to using service account impersonation with signed JWTs (longer-lived exchange tokens but tighter scopes)

jessie: quick mitigation: update the gitlab-runner helm values to set `oidc_id_token_lifetime: 90s` and restart runners. also add validator tolerance of 10s in the exchange config. we'll roll those in staging only first. can infra patch now? @irina

irina: I can patch staging values and restart the helmrelease. doing now. will monitor pipelines.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline #4823 for my-app/staging cancelled (user request)

sam: after the patch I re-ran one pipeline and it progressed past the secret-fetch step. staging deploy completed. thanks.

jessie: long-term action items:
1) eng-infra: align runner default token TTL across clusters to >=60s and include config validation in our cluster module templates.
2) eng-security: evaluate whether exchange validator tolerance change is acceptable (audit change, add telemetry). @mike
3) devex/support: update docs and quickstart note about minimum OIDC token lifetime for CI runners.

mike: +1 on the action items. also suggest we add an automated regression test — spin up a runner with 30s ttl and run secret fetch to ensure we detect this in e2e.

sam: for immediate follow-up: I created a temporary pipeline variable with a short-lived manual token to unblock a hotfix earlier (we rotated and revoked after deploy). recorded in the incident ticket: <https://tickets.example.com/INC-1923>

irina: created PR to set 90s in staging helm values and opened rollout change: https://git.example.com/infra/charts/merge-request/789. will coordinate with SRE for canary.

jessie: thanks everyone. marking this resolved for staging after rollout; keeping open for prod verification. if anyone sees regression please re-open thread. :thumbsup:
